NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 5 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, October 11 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 11, 3:18 PM ET

Trey McBride is the top-projected tight end on the Week 5 DraftKings main slate at 20.7 DraftKings points for $6,700, against Detroit. Brock Bowers (17.8, $7,000) and Sam LaPorta (14.1, $4,900) are next.

Trey McBride is also the top value at the position: 3.09 projected points per $1,000.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 11, 3:18 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 5

Trey McBride, ARI vs DET ($6,700)

Trey McBride carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 20.7 DraftKings points at $6,700, the 4th-highest on the entire main slate. That is 2.9 points clear of Brock Bowers. The model gives him 11.1 targets on 36.7 routes. The salary works out to 3.09 projected points per $1,000, 1st of 22 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 20.8 points with a simulated floor of 8.3 and a ceiling of 42.7, and he holds 29% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 5.5-point underdog at home against Detroit, with an implied team total of 25 in a game totaled at 55.5.

Brock Bowers, LV at NE ($7,000)

Brock Bowers projects 2nd at the position with 17.8 DraftKings points at $7,000. The model gives him 8.1 targets on 27.1 routes. The salary works out to 2.54 projected points per $1,000, 10th of 22 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Bowers averaged 17.9 points with a simulated floor of 6.7 and a ceiling of 37.0, and he holds 11% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 3.5-point underdog on the road against New England, with an implied team total of 21 in a game totaled at 45.5.

Value: Greg Dulcich, MIA vs CIN ($3,100)

Greg Dulcich projects for 8.6 DraftKings points at $3,100, which works out to 2.77 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 22 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 4.3 targets on 19.2 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Dulcich averaged 8.6 points with a simulated floor of 0.8 and a ceiling of 24.2, and he holds 4% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Miami is a 7-point underdog at home against Cincinnati, with an implied team total of 18.75 in a game totaled at 44.5.
